dedupe_keys.name: deep learning detection of heavy duty trucks and containers in satellite images southern california

description: This framework, published by Liu, Li, Sizemore, Xie and Wu in IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems (2024), detects heavy-duty trucks and shipping containers in satellite images by combining imagery with OpenStreetMap GIS data, so that trucks can be mapped both on and off the road over wide areas. Coverage: part of Southern California including the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. The method modifies the CenterNet detection algorithm to find randomly oriented trucks, ensembles it with the Mask R-CNN segmentation algorithm, and uses GIS information to refine predictions. The results support assessment of heavy-duty truck effects on port-adjacent communities and of truck density along major freight corridors. Format and access: an open access article, with a copy in PubMed Central. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one region; image dates and resolution limit what can be counted, and the code is not described in the abstract. The detections can calibrate truck volumes and parking demand in freight network flow and exposure models around ports. It relates to the truck traffic satellite monitoring model and OpenStreetMap in the catalogue.
